# pyautogui-agent

Agent-friendly companion layer on top of PyAutoGUI. PyAutoGUI only
understands pixels; this package adds structured screen elements,
one-call observation, waits with deadlines, task-level actions, and a
safety layer. It never modifies PyAutoGUI or PyScreeze. It only calls
them.

Install: pip install pyautogui-agent
OCR (optional): pip install "pyautogui-agent[ocr]" plus the Tesseract binary
macOS element listing (optional): pip install "pyautogui-agent[macos]"
Windows element listing (optional): pip install "pyautogui-agent[windows]"
Linux element listing: sudo apt install python3-pyatspi at-spi2-core
(pyatspi is not on PyPI, so there is no pip extra for it)

Import: import pyautogui_agent
All public names are available from pyautogui_agent directly, for
example: from pyautogui_agent import observe, click_text, Session.

## Observation

- observe(include_elements=True, take_screenshot=True, scale=None)
  Returns Observation with fields: screenshot (Pillow image or None),
  screen_size (width, height), mouse_position (x, y), elements
  (ElementListing or None), timestamp. On platforms without an element
  provider the listing is included with supported=False, never omitted.

## Elements (three providers, one shape)

- list_elements(max_depth=12, max_elements=500, scale=None)
  Returns ElementListing with fields: elements (list of Element),
  supported (bool), platform, message, scale (backing factor used),
  app_name (focused application, macOS only). Dispatches by
  platform to a provider; each returns the same ElementListing and
  Element shape with the same depth and count limits. When a
  provider's dependency is missing, the listing has supported=False
  with a clear install message, never a crash and never a silent
  empty list.
- Providers:
  - macOS: Accessibility API via pyobjc (scale is the display
    backing factor, Retina 2.0). Lists the focused application
    only. UNVERIFIED: implemented from the API specification, never
    run on a Mac.
  - Linux: AT-SPI via pyatspi (positions are already screen pixels,
    so scale is accepted but ignored). Lists the whole desktop, all
    applications. VERIFIED LIVE under Xvfb with a GTK dialog: tree,
    roles, names, sizes, and positions all correct, and a click on
    the listed OK button dismissed the dialog. Position detail:
    getPosition(XY_SCREEN) returns (0, 0) for descendants, so the
    provider takes a top-level window's screen position from
    XY_SCREEN and computes each descendant as that plus its own
    XY_WINDOW offset. Needs a D-Bus session bus; without one the
    listing is unsupported (libatspi aborts the process if getDesktop
    is called with no bus).
  - Windows: UI Automation via comtypes. UNVERIFIED: implemented
    from the API specification, cannot be tested on Linux.
- Element fields: role (for example "AXButton" on macOS,
  "push button" on Linux AT-SPI), title, description, position
  (x, y) in PyAutoGUI pixel coordinates, size (width, height),
  center (x, y), enabled (bool), value, visible (bool).
  Coordinates are Accessibility points scaled by the display backing
  scale factor (Retina: 2.0) on macOS. Pass scale= to override.
- find_element(role=None, title=None, title_contains=None,
  description=None, max_depth=12, max_elements=500, scale=None)
  Returns the first matching Element or None. Raises
  NotSupportedError on platforms without an element provider.
- find_all(...) same filters, returns a list (possibly empty).
- click_element(element, session=None) clicks the element center
  through the safety layer.

## Waits

- wait_for_image(image, timeout=10.0, interval=0.5, confidence=None,
  region=None, screenshot_dir=None)
  Returns the box (left, top, width, height) when the image appears.
  Raises ActionTimeoutError carrying last_screenshot (path) and waited.
  Confidence rule: when confidence is not None and OpenCV is not
  installed, raises ProviderNotInstalledError("OpenCV", ...) with
  the install hint (pip install opencv-python); without OpenCV only
  exact matching is available. A raw NotImplementedError from
  locateOnScreen is converted to the same error.
- wait_for_condition(fn, timeout=10.0, interval=0.5,
  description="condition", screenshot_dir=None)
  Returns the truthy value fn() returns. Raises ActionTimeoutError
  carrying last_screenshot on timeout.

## Actions (all go through a safety Session)

- click_text(text, timeout=10.0, interval=1.0, session=None,
  language="eng", screenshot_dir=None)
  Finds text on screen with OCR and clicks its center. Returns the
  (x, y) center, or None in dry-run mode. Raises
  ElementNotFoundError (query, screenshot_path, closest_match,
  confidence) when the text never appears, and
  ProviderNotInstalledError when Tesseract is absent. OCR detail:
  the screenshot is upscaled 2x and read with Tesseract psm 11
  (sparse text), because the default page segmentation missed small
  labels such as a 16pt "Name:" next to an entry field. Coordinates
  are scaled back to screen pixels. Each OCR pass takes about 2
  seconds on a 1920x1080 screen.
- fill_field(text, value, session=None, timeout=10.0, interval=0.05,
  field_gap=30)
  Clicks a field by its label (accessibility element first, then OCR
  text) and types the value. Raises ElementNotFoundError when the
  label cannot be found. Field-point heuristic (OCR path): the
  label's box is found, then the click lands on the FIELD, not the
  label: the point to the right of the label on the same row,
  (label_right + field_gap, label_center_y), with field_gap
  defaulting to 30px. When the label spans nearly the full screen
  width (no room to the right), the fallback is below the label,
  (label_center_x, label_bottom + field_gap). The accessibility
  path (macOS) clicks the real field element and does not use this
  heuristic.
- click_image(image, session=None, timeout=10.0, interval=0.5,
  confidence=None, region=None)
  Waits for an image, then clicks its center. Returns (x, y) or None
  in dry-run mode. Raises ActionTimeoutError when the image never
  appears.
- click_point(x, y, button="left", session=None)
  Clicks a point through the safety layer. Prefer click_text,
  click_image, or click_element when the target can be named.

## Safety

- Session(dry_run=False, confirm_hook=None, confirm_predicate=None)
  dry_run=True logs actions without executing them.
  confirm_hook is a callable taking an ActionRecord and returning True
  to allow or False to decline an action. confirm_predicate selects
  which actions need confirmation; when None and a hook is set, the
  hook is consulted for every action. A declined action raises
  ActionDeclinedError and is not executed.
- Session.execute(action, args, fn, result_summary=None) runs fn
  under the session rules and logs it. Returns fn() result, or None
  in dry-run mode.
- Session.dry_run_mode() context manager: temporarily enable dry-run.
- dry_run() context manager: same, on the default session.
- get_default_session() / set_default_session(session).
- Session.log is a list of ActionRecord with fields: timestamp,
  action, args, result, executed, declined.
- Session.format_log() returns printable lines. Session.last_action()
  returns the most recent record or None.

## Errors (all derive from AgentError)

- ElementNotFoundError: query, screenshot_path, closest_match,
  confidence.
- ActionTimeoutError: what, timeout, waited, last_screenshot.
- ProviderNotInstalledError: provider, install_hint.
- NotSupportedError: feature, platform, detail.
- ActionDeclinedError: action, action_args.
- DisplayUnavailableError: raised when PyAutoGUI cannot connect to a
  display (headless machine). Importing this package never raises it;
  only actions that need the screen do.

## Rules for agents using this package

- Never call raw pyautogui functions when a task-level action exists.
  Prefer click_text, fill_field, click_image, click_element.
- Always pass a Session. Use Session(dry_run=True) while testing a
  new task, and keep the confirmation hook on for destructive actions.
- Always check obs.elements.supported before trusting an empty
  element list. An empty list on an unsupported platform means "no
  provider", not "no elements".
- On ElementNotFoundError or ActionTimeoutError, read screenshot_path
  and look at the screenshot before retrying. The screenshot shows
  what the screen actually looked like.
- Coordinates are top-left origin, X right, Y down, primary display
  only (a PyAutoGUI limit). Never hardcode coordinates from another
  machine; use observe() or the element list.
- locate-based calls are slow (1 to 2 seconds each). Do not poll in a
  loop; use wait_for_image or wait_for_condition.

## Verification status

- Waits, errors, safety, dry-run, action log, and observe() structure
  are unit tested with mocks, no display needed. 66 unit tests pass.
- Linux AT-SPI element listing is verified live under Xvfb with a
  GTK dialog (tree, roles, names, sizes, positions, and a real click
  that dismissed the dialog). OCR clicking and fill_field are
  verified live on this VM (9 of 9 live checks pass, real scrot
  screenshot path). See TESTING.md.
- macOS element listing and Windows UI Automation are implemented
  from API specifications and are UNVERIFIED. Verify macOS with
  scripts/mac_live_test.py on the owner's Mac before relying on it.
